exampleAnswers.title: Describing Properties of the Secant Function

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\sec x?$

  1. $x = -\dfrac{7\pi}{2}$ is not in the domain of the function.
  2. $y = 10$ is in the range of the function. $\phantom{\dfrac{7\pi}{2}}$
  3. $x = \dfrac{\pi}{8}$ is a vertical asymptote.
question.explanation:
Let's plot the graph of $y=\sec x.$

Let's go through each statement.

  • Statement I is true. The function is defined for all real numbers except the values $\dfrac\pi 2 + n\pi$ for any integer $n,$ thus it is not defined for $x=-\dfrac{7\pi}{2}.$

  • Statement II is true. The range of the function is $(-\infty, -1] \cup [1, \infty),$ so $y=10$ is in the range.

  • Statement III is false. The function $y=\sec x$ has vertical asymptotes at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}+n\pi$, thus $x=\dfrac{\pi}{8}$ is not a vertical asymptote.

example.title: Describing Properties of the Secant Function

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\sec x?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.

  1. The function has vertical asymptotes at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}+n\pi$
  2. The graph of the function passes through the point $(0,0)$
  3. It is an odd function
question.explanation:
Let's plot the graph of $y=\sec x.$

Let's go through each statement.

  • Statement I is true. The function $y=\sec{x}$ has vertical asymptotes at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}+n\pi.$

  • Statement II is false. Since $\sec{0} = 1,$ the graph of the function $y = \sec{x}$ passes through the point $(0,1).$

  • Statement III is false. The graph of the function does not have rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. Thus, $y = \sec{x}$ is not an odd function.

exampleAnswers.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Secant Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \sec x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have \[ \sec{x} = \sec(x + 2n\pi). \]

Substituting $n=4$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives \begin{align*} \sec{x} = \sec(x + 2\cdot 4\cdot\pi) = \sec(x + 8\pi). \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\sec{x} = 3\sqrt{3},$ then $\sec(x + 8\pi) = 3\sqrt{3}.$

example.title: Utilizing the Periodicity Property of the Secant Function

question.explanation:
The period of $y = \sec x$ is $2\pi.$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have \[ \sec{x} = \sec(x + 2n\pi). \]

Substituting $n=-9$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives \begin{align*} \sec{x} = \sec(x + 2\cdot (-9) \cdot\pi) = \sec(x-18\pi). \end{align*}

Therefore, if $\sec{x} = \dfrac{7}{6},$ then $\sec(x - 18\pi) =\dfrac{7}{6}.$

Finally, then \begin{align} 18\sec(x - 18\pi) + 2 &= 18 \left(\dfrac{7}{6} \right) +2 \\[5pt] & = 21 +2 \\[5pt] &= 23 . \end{align}

exampleAnswers.title: Utilizing the Evenness Property of the Secant Function

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the graph of $y = \sec{x}.$

From the graph, we note the following:

  • The period of $\sec{x}$ is $2\pi.$

  • Our graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis. This means that $\sec{x}$ is an even function, and we have \[ \sec(-x) = \sec{x}. \]

Let's now evaluate our expression:

  • Firstly, using the periodicity of $\sec{x},$ we have \begin{align} \sec(-x + 8\pi) & = \sec(-x + 2\pi \cdot 4) \\[5pt] & = \sec(-x). \end{align}

  • Secondly, using the evenness of $\sec{x},$ we have \begin{align} \sec(-x) & = \sec{x} \\[5pt] & = -\dfrac{5}{3}. \end{align}

Therefore, \begin{align} 6\sec(-x + 8\pi) + 7 & = 6\left(-\dfrac{5}{3}\right) + 7\\[5pt] & = -10 + 7\\[5pt] & = -3. \end{align}

example.title: Utilizing the Evenness Property of the Secant Function

question.explanation:
First, let's recall the graph of $y = \sec{x}.$

From the graph, we note the following:

  • The period of $\sec{x}$ is $2\pi.$

  • Our graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis. This means that $\sec{x}$ is an even function, and we have \[ \sec(-x) = \sec{x}. \]

Let's now evaluate our expression:

  • Firstly, using the periodicity of $\sec{x},$ we have \begin{align} \sec(-x - 10\pi) & = \sec(-x - 2\pi \cdot 5) \\[5pt] & = \sec(-x). \end{align}

  • Secondly, using the evenness of $\sec{x},$ we have \begin{align} \sec(-x) & = \sec{x} \\[5pt] & = 3. \end{align}

Therefore, \begin{align} 3\sec(-x - 10\pi) - 5 & = 3\left(3\right) - 5\\[5pt] & = 9 - 5\\[5pt] & = 4. \end{align}
